newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall on pre-election jitters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall on pre-election jitters.

text.p: French shares fell on Tuesday on election jitters but recovered from the day's lows on expectations the conservatives would win a snap parliamentary poll called by President Jacques Chirac.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down eight points or 0.32 percent at 2,514.67, well above the day's low of 2,487.80.
Volume was 9.2 billion francs, inflated by block trades.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down eight at 2,515.

"The market's a bit afraid of everything though it appears the Right has a good chance of winning, albeit with a smaller majority," one trader said, adding investors believed there was not much chance of the Left taking power.
Brokers said the market would be driven by polls from now until the May 25 first round of voting in the election. Run-offs in the two-round poll are set for June 1.

The bourse, which had closed down for the two prior sessions, opened higher in a technical rebound but turned negative on anxiety about the election outcome and a four-week delay in the partial privatisation of France Telecom.
Prices later derived some support from an early rise on Wall Street and from firmer bond prices.

The Finance Ministry said it was putting off the start of the France Telecom privatisation to early June. It said the timetable for privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF would not be affected.
Thomson-CSF shares, which had fallen on Monday on concerns that the election would delay the sale of the state's 58-percent stake, finished up 1.51 percent at 181.30 francs.

Shares in Clarins fell 6.53 percent to 701 francs after the skin-care firm did not rule out a share issue to fund an acquisition, brokers said. On Monday it posted net attributable profits of 241.2 million francs for 1996, up 17.5 percent.
Renault shares rose 3.29 percent to 132 francs. One broker said the stock has benefitted from the perception that the car-maker has taken concrete steps to tackle its problems.
